script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - EARLY MORNING

A peaceful, picturesque small town. Dew on the grass. Birds chirping. The sun slowly rising.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(wistful)
In a small town like ours, life is simple. But sometimes, the simplest things can hide the most complex stories.

CUT TO:

INT. HIGH SCHOOL CAFETERIA - DAY

STUDENTS are scattered at tables, chattering amongst themselves. The bell rings, signaling the end of lunch. They start to gather their things and head to their next class.

At a corner table, a group of STUDENT-ATHLETES sit, looking tense and anxious. They share worried glances.

Suddenly, the principal's voice echoes through the PA system.

PRINCIPAL (V.O.)
(serious)
Attention, students. Due to unforeseen circumstances, the school budget has been cut. Effective immediately, all sports teams will be disbanded.

The student-athletes exchange looks of disbelief.

CUT TO:

EXT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL FIELD - LATER

The student-athletes gather on the empty football field, their faces etched with determination.

COACH (standing before them)
(firm)
We can't let our team die. We have to find a way to keep playing.

The students nod in agreement.

SCENE 2 - THE FUNDING CAMPAIGN

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The student-athletes are huddled around a table, brainstorming ideas to raise funds for their team.

JENNY (passionate)
We could sell merchandise, like T-shirts and hats!

MICHAEL (skeptical)
(realistic)
How many people in this small town are gonna buy that stuff?

JENNY (determined)
We'll make it work. We'll reach out to local businesses for sponsorships, too.

CUT TO:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - DAY

The students go door-to-door, seeking donations and sponsorships. Some are receptive, while others are skeptical.

SCENE 3 - THE FIRST SUCCESS

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The students are gathered around the table once more, this time with a sense of accomplishment.

JENNY (smiling)
We did it! The local hardware store agreed to sponsor us!

They all cheer and high-five each other.

CUT TO:

EXT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL FIELD - EVENING

The students practice under the lights, their spirits lifted by their recent success.

SCENE 4 - A SETBACK

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The students sit around the table, their faces somber.

MRS. JENKINS (the school principal) enters.

MRS. JENKINS
(apologetic)
I've received some distressing news. Due to budget cuts, the school is unable to provide us with the use of the football field.

The students are crestfallen.

CUT TO:

EXT. PARK - DAY

The students practice in the park, making the best of a difficult situation.

SCENE 5 - THE BIG GAME

EXT. OUTSKIRTS OF TOWN - EVENING

The students face off against another small-town team in a make-shift stadium, built from scraps and donations.

They play with determination and heart, overcoming their adversities.

SCENE 6 - THE WIN

EXT. OUTSKIRTS OF TOWN - NIGHT

The students celebrate their victory, exhausted but triumphant.

CUT TO:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - MORNING

The sun rises over the small town, casting a golden glow over the peaceful scene.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(reflective)
In a world where budgets are cut and dreams seem impossible, these students proved that anything is possible with determination, hard work, and the support of their community.

FADE OUT.
